medicaid_program_name: Delaware Medicaid (Diamond State Health Plan), run by the Division of Medicaid & Medical Assistance (DMMA), Delaware Department of Health and Social Services; adults are covered through the Adult Medicaid Expansion group
medicaid_adult_income_limit_note: DMMA Medicaid ENGAGE page: the Adult Medicaid Expansion group 'includes low-income adults, ages 19 through 64 ... with household incomes up to 133% of the federal poverty level.' DMMA's '2026 Countable Income Limits for Federal Poverty Level Related Medical Assistance Programs' table lists 133% FPL monthly income of $1,769 for a family of 1 and $3,658 for a family of 4 (table labeled 2026; no exact effective day shown on the page). 2027 work requirement announced by the state: 'Starting January 1, 2027, you must work and earn at least $580 a month or complete at least 80 hours a month' (working, volunteering/community service, a work program, or school/job training at least part-time), with exemptions; six-month renewals for the expansion group also start January 1, 2027. Non-citizen eligibility changes started October 1, 2026.
medicaid_quote: New federal work and community engagement requirements for those in the Medicaid Expansion group go into effect January 1, 2027.
medicaid_quote_2: Under the Affordable Care Act, the Medicaid Expansion group includes low-income adults, ages 19 through 64 ... with household incomes up to 133% of the federal poverty level.
medicaid_quote_3: Starting January 1, 2027, you must work and earn at least $580 a month or complete at least 80 hours a month

state_subsidy_or_reinsurance_note: Delaware Health Insurance Individual Market Stabilization Reinsurance Program (Section 1332 state reinsurance waiver), in place since plan year 2020. CMS approved a five-year extension effective January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2029, so the program's federal approval covers plan year 2027. Funded by federal pass-through money plus a 2.75% carrier assessment collected by the DOI; administered by the Delaware Health Care Commission. No state-funded premium subsidy (separate from the federal tax credit) was found on the DOI or exchange pages checked.
state_subsidy_quote: On July 31, 2024, CMS approved the extension, extending the Reinsurance Program waiver period from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2029
state_subsidy_quote_2: CMS 1332 page: "This approval is effective for January 1, 2025, through December 31, 2029." (original approval "effective for January 1, 2020 through December 31, 2024")

copy.medicaid: Delaware has expanded Medicaid. Adults age 19 through 64 with household income up to 133% of the federal poverty level can qualify. The state’s 2026 table puts that at $1,769 a month for one person. Starting January 1, 2027, adults in this group must meet a work rule unless they are exempt. They must earn at least $580 a month or spend at least 80 hours a month in work, volunteering, a work program, or school or job training.
copy.state_help: Delaware has a state reinsurance program for individual health plans. It pays insurers back for part of their high-cost claims. It has been in place since 2020, and its federal approval runs through December 31, 2029.

notes_unverified: DMMA's income-limits page labels its table '2026' but shows no exact effective date; the 133% column is not itself labeled 'adult expansion'. The 133% figure comes from the ENGAGE page definition of the expansion group. Delaware states the limit as 133% (not 138%); copy follows the state's wording.

Delaware has historically been described as a State Partnership Marketplace (the state handles plan review; HealthCare.gov handles enrollment). The CMS page fetched has no partnership list, so that label was not verified for 2027 and is not used in copy.

Reinsurance: 2027-specific parameters (attachment point, cap, coinsurance) and the 2027 pass-through amount were not found; the Delaware Health Care Commission reinsurance page (dhss.delaware.gov/dhcc/reinsur1332waiver/) returned 404. Federal approval through 2029 is confirmed; actual 2027 operation is inferred from that approval and the March 2026 DOI bulletin, not from a 2027-specific notice.
No Delaware state-funded premium subsidy was found on the DOI, DHSS or HealthCare.gov pages checked; absence was not exhaustively verified.
The DOI rate release (Sept 4, 2026) contains carrier names and rate changes; none are used in copy per the content rules.
